## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage

# As the levels progress increase the number of enemies and decrease the number of power ups

## Problem statement

By level 5 the player has accumulated enough permanent weapon and power-up levels that they destroy enemies almost instantly, while the per-kill power-up supply is still the flat level-1 rate (18 %). Enemy density does not rise enough (and on level 5 is deliberately lower) to offset that firepower, so the mid/late campaign feels trivial and over-supplied rather than escalating.

## Users

- **Players** — "As a player, I expect each level to threaten me more than the last and to hand out fewer upgrades as I get stronger, so the campaign keeps its tension."
- **Gym users / balance engineers** — "As a balance engineer, I expect the level gym and the automated balance harness to reproduce the game's level-scaled enemy counts and drop rate, so tuning transfers to the shipped game."
- **Producers** — "As a producer, I want the change measured with before/after bot-batch evidence rather than a single hand-watched run."

## Goal

Make difficulty scale with the campaign level on two independent axes: **more enemies** and **fewer power-up drops per enemy**. Both axes are data-driven, shared with the gyms, deterministic, and evidence-backed by the automated balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Data-driven level-scaling curves** — A pure, Phaser-free shared module (proposed `src/core/levelScaling.ts`) exposes `enemyCountMultiplier(level)` and `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)` backed by tunable defaults (proposed: extend `GameRules`), with inputs clamped to the campaign range. Defaults: enemy-count multiplier **1.00 at L1 → 2.00 at L10** (linear across 1–10); per-kill power-up drop chance **0.18 at L1 → 0.05 at L10** (monotonically non-increasing); the small-asteroid Extra Life chance scales by the same ratio. Level 1 values reproduce today's behaviour exactly.
- **Enemy counts rise with level** — Campaign waves built for levels 1–10 have each group's `count` multiplied by `enemyCountMultiplier(level)`, rounded with a documented rule, floored at 1, capped by a documented per-group safety limit (≤ 200, the existing formation cap), with `single`-formation groups left at exactly 1. Level 1 wave data is byte-identical to today. The scaling applies to both the static `LEVELS` campaign and the sequenced campaign; same-seed builds remain byte-identical (determinism contract preserved) and the scaled campaign still satisfies the existing campaign invariants and wave-balance rules (AH-0MV84TE7O006HI3R).
- **Power-up supply per enemy falls with level** — Every kill-time drop roll in `PlayScene` uses the per-level chance, so the L10 per-kill drop chance is **≤ 30 % of the L1 chance**; the Extra Life roll scales proportionally. Drop types/weights and the timed weapon/power-up effects are unchanged; L1 drop behaviour is unchanged.
- **Gym parity** — The same scaling helper is used by the level-based gyms (`GymLevel`, hence `GymBotTuning`, and the curve-sequencer launch path) so a launched level produces the same enemy counts as the game, and the level-gym supply cadence is lengthened by the inverse drop-chance ratio so high-level gym runs are not over-supplied. Formation gyms keep their documented scene-specific supply source (no campaign level context) and are unchanged; the divergence is recorded in the work item and a code comment. A parity test asserts game campaign and level-gym counts match for the same level.
- **Automated balance evidence** — The deterministic evaluation harness can measure the change (extend the arena/batch so a run can exercise the real campaign waves and the real per-kill drop rule, at least for L1/L5/L10). Record a same-seed **baseline batch (100 games, competent policy)** against HEAD and a **post-change batch** in the work item or `docs/BALANCING.md`, including per-level `powerUpsCollected`, `enemiesKilledByArchetype`, `avoidableHits`, `survivalSeconds` and `levelReached`. The evidence must show the mid/late-level power-up supply per enemy is below baseline and that the campaign remains playable (no crash, no fall in the batch's reached-level/completion metric).
- **Tests** — Unit tests cover curve monotonicity/clamping, count application (rounding, `single` groups, caps, L1 identity, seeded determinism), per-level drop chance, Extra Life proportionality and game↔gym parity. New tests fail on the pre-change code and pass after it.
- **Documentation** — `docs/BALANCING.md` (scaling table + evidence), the GDD power-up/level sections and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (if the wave-build seam changes) are updated with the new behaviour and tuning rationale; code comments document the curves.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory** (repo `AGENTS.md`): enabled gameplay behaviour is shared code, consumed by the game and every relevant gym; only a documented disabled feature may diverge.
- **Determinism:** the `curve`/`fixed` wave determinism contract and same-seed reproducibility must not change.
- **Level 1 onboarding is untouched** — the multiplier and drop chance at L1 are exactly today's values, so the opening calibration, tests and balance baseline remain valid.
- **No changes to enemy archetype stats or behaviours, and no changes to the permanent weapon/power-up level economy** — this item adjusts enemy density and drop supply only. Any retuning of upgrade strength is separate scope.
- **Backwards-compatible rules persistence** — existing `localStorage` rule blobs must load with the new defaults merged in; no schema break.
- **No new player-facing UI** — the curves are tuning data, not a settings screen.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene` drops a power-up on every kill with a flat `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE = 0.18` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`), plus a flat `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` (default 0.05 in `src/core/rules.ts`). Neither reads the campaign level.
- Enemy counts are hand-authored per wave in `LEVELS` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`), merged with curve-generated waves by `buildSequencedLevels` (`src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`). `resolveCampaignLevels` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`) chooses static vs sequenced. There is no level-based count multiplier anywhere.
- Level 5 is authored as "fewer enemies, structured patterns" (4–10 Phasers), while the player's permanent upgrades have accumulated — the reported over-supply peak.
- `powerUpSpawnInterval` (default 12.5 s) drives the gym supply cadence (`GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`); the game does not use it.
- The formation count cap was raised to 200 (AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5), so larger scaled formations are representable.
- The automated balance harness (`src/ai/eval/`, `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, `docs/BALANCING.md`) simulates a single-level skirmish and **seeds** power-ups; it does not currently exercise the kill-chance drop rule or per-level campaign waves, so measuring this change needs a harness extension.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure level-scaling module with the two curves and their data defaults, clamped and documented.
2. Apply the enemy-count multiplier at the shared campaign-build seam (and the level-gym launch seam) so game and gym counts match.
3. Replace the flat kill-drop roll (and proportional Extra Life roll) in `PlayScene` with the level-resolved chance.
4. Align the level-gym supply cadence with the same curve.
5. Extend the balance harness to exercise the real campaign/drop rule and record baseline vs post-change evidence.
6. Update tests and docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/levelScaling.ts` — **New.** Pure `enemyCountMultiplier`, `powerUpDropChance`, count-application helper and defaults; the single source of truth for both axes.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — Add the tunable scaling data to `GameRules` with defaults, validation/clamping and backwards-compatible loading; expose defaults for tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Apply the count scaling to the campaign (both static and sequenced paths) and use the level-resolved drop chance in `_maybeDropPowerUp`; scale the Extra Life roll.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` / `src/waves/Formations.ts` — Shared seam (or a helper consumed by it) where campaign counts are scaled after composition, preserving `single` groups and determinism.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — Apply the same count scaling on launch and derive the supply cadence from the level's drop chance.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts`, `src/ai/eval/types.ts`, `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — Extend the deterministic run so campaign waves and the kill-chance drop rule participate, and the batch reports per-level evidence.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/waves/*.test.ts`, `src/core/rules.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts`, `src/ai/eval/*.test.ts` — Curve, application, determinism, parity and harness coverage.
- `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Scaling table, rationale and before/after evidence.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** a linear enemy-count ramp to 2.0× at L10 and a per-kill drop ramp to 0.05 are reasonable starting values; the exact values are tuning data and may be adjusted from the bot-batch evidence without changing the design.
- **Assumption:** scaling every wave (including mini-boss waves) is correct; the safety cap and formation bounds keep enlarged groups playable.
- **Risk:** doubling large formations may overflow the arena or hurt readability; mitigations are the 200-count cap, a per-wave/formation bounds test and bot-batch survival evidence.
- **Risk:** reducing drops may starve the player at levels where enemy count scaling cannot offset the loss (notably L5's small authored waves); mitigate by keeping the L5 drop chance higher than the linear endpoint and confirming with the bot batch.
- **Risk:** the evaluation harness extension is a non-trivial change to a shared tool; keep it additive (optional per-level mode) so existing batch artifacts stay compatible.
- **Risk:** `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE` is an exported constant with tests/references; keep it as the documented L1 base value and derive higher levels from it so existing imports do not silently change meaning.
- **Scope-creep guard:** do not retune weapon/power-up level effects, drop weights, enemy archetypes, or the permanent-upgrade economy in this item; capture such opportunities as separate work items.
- **Documented divergence:** formation gyms have no campaign-level context, so their fixed-cadence supply stays as-is; only the level-based gyms adopt the level curve.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** (completed) — retuned the default difficulty curve and seeded campaign for playability; this item tunes the complementary enemy-density/drop-supply axis.
- **AH-0MV395QHS004SCOR** / **AH-0MVCYANT6003SG5C** (completed) — extended the campaign to 10 levels with hand-authored fixed waves; the count multiplier must preserve those authored identities.
- **AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5** (completed) — raised the formation enemy cap to 200, which makes scaled counts feasible.
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** (completed) — designed the power-up level curves (the permanent-strength side of the imbalance).
- **AH-0MV81Z2EJ006HD5T** (completed) — delivered the automated balancing batch harness that this item extends for evidence.
- **AH-0MV84TE7O006HI3R** — pure wave-balance rules (R1–R3) and audit; the scaled counts must still satisfy the campaign invariants.
- Repo `AGENTS.md` — gym↔game parity convention.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — automated balance harness and statistics schema.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)
- **AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5** – Increase the possible number of enemies in a enemy formation to 200 (completed)
- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** – Add a Magnet power up (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: destroying, dropped, drops, enemies, everything (+15 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: destroying, dropped, drops, enemies, get (+15 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: destroying, dropped, drops, enemies, everything (+13 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — How should power-up supply decrease with level?** Options: (A) data-driven per-level drop-chance curve (e.g. 18 % at L1 tapering to ~5–6 % at L10) with Extra Life scaled; (B) a single global cut; (C) add a drop throttle. — **Answer (operator): A.** Source: interactive reply. The curve is the single tunable place; Extra Life follows the same ratio.
- **Q2 — How should enemy numbers increase with level?** Options: (A) a data-driven level-based enemy-count multiplier applied when waves are built; (B) re-author static counts by hand; (C) raise only curve targets. — **Answer (operator): A.** Source: interactive reply. Applies to both fixed and curve waves and avoids re-authoring 100 waves.
- **Q3 — How should "not overpowered" be verified?** Options: (A) automated balance-evaluation evidence (bot batch: power-up pickups per run and survival trend across levels) plus unit tests for the curves; (B) deterministic unit tests only; (C) manual play-test only. — **Answer (operator): A.** Source: interactive reply. Research: the current harness seeds power-ups and plays a single-level skirmish, so this item must extend it to exercise the real campaign/drop rule for the evidence to be meaningful.
## Plan (decomposition — 2026-10-23)

Planned by the plan skill. Eleven children in test-first dependency order; each
test item precedes the implementation item it pins, and every child carries the
parent ACs it satisfies under "Parent AC traceability".

**Phase 1 — Scaling contract (vertical slice: module + rules + tests + docs)**
- T1 — Write level-scaling curve and rules contract tests (AH-0MVLJCYGW001TRB3)
- F1 — Add level-scaling module and tunable rules (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X)

**Phase 2 — Campaign density (slice: build seam + determinism/invariant tests)**
- T2 — Write scaled-campaign determinism and invariant tests (AH-0MVLJF1PO000PB21)
- F2 — Apply enemy-count scaling at campaign build seam (AH-0MVLJF30O000E3J3)

**Phase 3 — Drop supply (slice: PlayScene roll + seeded RNG tests)**
- T3 — Write per-level kill-drop chance tests (AH-0MVLJF4DI000BKMQ)
- F3 — Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene (AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X)

**Phase 4 — Gym parity (slice: gym launch + parity tests + documented divergence)**
- T4 — Write level-gym parity tests (AH-0MVLJF6ZD00164MG)
- F4 — Scale level-gym counts and supply cadence (AH-0MVLJF886009584F)

**Phase 5 — Balance evidence (slice: harness mode + per-level report + batch evidence + docs)**
- T5 — Write balance-harness per-level mode tests (AH-0MVLJF9HC007AOI6)
- F5 — Extend balance harness for per-level campaign runs (AH-0MVLJFB1I0099X4Z)
- D1 — Record bot-batch evidence and scaling docs (AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H)

Dependency edges (dependent ← prerequisite):
- F1 ← T1; T2 ← F1; F2 ← T2; T3 ← F1; F3 ← T3
- T4 ← F2, F3; F4 ← T4
- T5 ← F1, F2, F3; F5 ← T5
- D1 ← F2, F3, F4, F5

**Vertical-slice check:** each phase pair is a complete slice (shared helper or
scene change + tests + code comments/docs in the same change). Phase 5 is the
one deliberately horizontal-looking slice: it needs the campaign and drop seams
from phases 2–3 before it can measure them, and it carries its own tests and
the evidence documentation.

**Between phases:** review the next phase's items and update their descriptions
with anything learned (e.g. the exact rounding rule, the `LevelDefinition.level`
launch seam) before starting them.

**Documented assumptions adopted at planning time (from the parent ACs, not new
requirements):**
- Round-half-up is the count rounding rule (`Math.round`), with a floor of 1 and
  a per-group cap of 200; `single`-formation groups stay at exactly 1.
- Both curves are linear across levels 1–10 with endpoints 1.00→2.00 (count) and
  0.18→0.05 (per-kill drop chance); Extra Life follows the drop-chance ratio.
- Single-wave gym launches (`level: 0`) are treated as level 1.
- The harness extension is additive: default skirmish/batch behaviour, schema
  and seeds are unchanged; baseline evidence is captured with the curves
  disabled in the same harness.

**Open items carried to implementation:** none blocking. Risk noted at planning
time — phase 5 may split into "arena mode" and "batch reporting" if the arena
change turns out to be large; that split is an implementation decision, not a
planning gap.

**Plan: changelog**
- 2026-10-23 — plan skill run: effort/risk pre-check returned `plan`; approval
  gate returned `request_approval: false` (Medium effort / High risk at the
  time), so no approval pause. Duplicate-work check found no overlapping item.
  Created 11 children with dependency edges; converted `Key Files` sections to
  the machine-validated format; AC coverage review returned 100 % coverage
  (`proceed`).


### Plan-session follow-up (2026-10-23)

No additional clarifying questions were required: Q1–Q3 above already pin the
approach (data-driven curves, level-based count multiplier, bot-batch
verification), and the remaining parameters were fixed by the acceptance
criteria themselves (endpoints, rounding, cap, `single` handling, gym
divergence). The parameters adopted are recorded in the "Plan (decomposition)"
section as explicit assumptions so implementation does not silently invent
requirements.

**Questions asked this session:** none (all answered questions recorded above).

# Test: wrapAware config plumbing

Test-first verification slice for the `wrapAware` parameter (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1 + AC5). Pins the data-driven boolean's default, seed exclusions, CSV wiring and editor exposure **before** the implementation item lands, so the pipeline change is driven by failing tests.

## Goal

Pin the full config pipeline for `wrapAware`: default `true`, `march`/`centipede` seeded `false`, CSV persist + round-trip, editor-panel visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts a generic archetype resolves `wrapAware === true` when the field is absent from its seed config.
- Tests assert the `march` and `centipede` seed configs carry `wrapAware === false` (the explicit exclusion list).
- A CSV round-trip test asserts a `wrapAware` column persists and reloads through the config CSV path; a missing/empty value falls back to `true`.
- A test asserts the field is enumerable through the existing `EnemyConfig` editor/config plumbing without extra per-field admin.
- All tests pass deterministically (no wall clock, no RNG).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`

# Intake brief: Upgrade text must reflect the actual upgrade for each weapon and level

## Problem statement

When the player is offered an upgrade, the on-screen text does not say what that
specific weapon or power-up actually gains at that level: every option shows the
same base-item description (identical for every weapon **and** every level), so
the choice is a blind guess. The secondary issue: even where a level-delta
summary is shown (hold-full choice), it is generated from shared curves with no
per-weapon filtering, so non-AoE weapons falsely report a "+N% AoE radius".

## Users

As a **player**, when I defeat a mini-boss and am offered an upgrade, or when I
fill my hold and choose a level-up, I want the option text to tell me what that
weapon/power-up gains at that specific next level — e.g. `+1 Projectiles, +17%
Fire rate` — and to never promise an effect the item does not have (e.g. AoE on
a non-AoE weapon).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 — Mini-boss reward upgrade options carry a level-accurate change summary
  (`changeSummary`) showing the real delta between the current level and the
  offered level (e.g. `+1 Projectiles, +17% Fire rate`), matching the deltas the
  hold-full choice already shows. Applies to every offered `weapon-level` and
  `power-up-level` option from `buildUpgradeOptions` (src/powerups/unlocks.ts),
  for weapons via `summariseWeaponLevelChange` and power-ups via
  `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`.
- AC2 — The change summary only lists variables that **actually change the game
  behaviour of that weapon/power-up** at that level: implemented (MVP) variables
  only; no unimplemented/planned variables; no `aoeRadius` delta on weapons
  without an `aoe` descriptor. Verified with a regression test that a non-AoE
  weapon never yields an "AoE" fragment.
- AC3 — The same option model is shared: both the mini-boss reward and the
  hold-full choice build level-up options through one code path (no divergent
  copies), so the text cannot drift between the game and the gyms
  (gym↔game parity — no gym shows mini-boss rewards, but `GymWeaponLeveling`
  consumes the shared hold-full candidates). The existing hold-full behaviour
  (level-accurate summary + `★ New` badge) must not regress.
- AC4 — Testing/validation: new unit tests cover (i) a weapon-level reward
  option carries a non-empty, level-accurate summary; (ii) a power-up-level
  reward option carries its summary; (iii) non-AoE weapons never report an AoE
  delta; (iv) summary text differs between levels where the maths differ. Full
  project test suite must pass.
- AC5 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (no
  catalogue changes are anticipated; the docs guards in `weaponLevelingDocs.test.ts`
  must still pass).

## Constraints

- Do not change upgrade maths, curves, caps, or the MVP variable set — display
  copy only.
- Do not surface 'planned'/unimplemented upgrade variables (damage, pierce,
  bounce, homing, chainCount, splitCount, critChance, statusChance,
  bulletSpeed, bulletLifetime, spreadAngle) in player-facing text.
- Keep deltas computed from the shared level maths (single source of truth —
  `summariseWeaponLevelChange` / `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`) — never
  hard-code numbers.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `buildChoiceCandidates` populates `changeSummary`
  for hold-full `weapon-level` / `power-up-level` offers (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR).
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` — `buildUpgradeOptions` (mini-boss reward,
  AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH) reuses `toChoiceOption` and **omits `changeSummary`**, so
  the overlay shows only the base catalogue description for every weapon/level.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `summariseWeaponLevelChange` iterates the 4 MVP
  variables (`fireRate`, `projectileCount`, `bulletSize`, `aoeRadius`) with no
  per-weapon applicability filter; `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` curves are shared by
  all weapons, so text is near-identical across weapons at the same level.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — renders the option name, description line
  and detail line (`'★ New'` or `changeSummary`); a missing `changeSummary`
  renders no detail line at all.
- Gyms: `GymWeaponLeveling`/`GymPowerUpLeveling` consume the shared hold-full
  candidates, so they inherit any fix automatically.

## Desired change

1. Populate `changeSummary` in `buildUpgradeOptions` for every owned
   `weapon-level`/`power-up-level` offer, using the same shared summarisers and
   the offered level (`level → level + 1`).
2. Extract a single "build level-up option" helper used by both
   `buildChoiceCandidates` and `buildUpgradeOptions` (parity AC3), or
   minimally have `buildUpgradeOptions` reuse the existing candidate builder.
3. Add per-weapon applicability filtering to the weapon change summary: skip
   `aoeRadius` when the weapon has no `aoe` descriptor (checked once per
   weapon); keep the implemented MVP variable set otherwise.
4. Add regression tests (`unlocks.test.ts`, `weaponLevels.test.ts`, and the
   `choice.test.ts` parity guard) covering the ACs above.

The base catalogue description line (`option.description`) stays as it is — it
tells the player what the item is; the new summary tells them what the level
gains.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` — `buildUpgradeOptions`: add `changeSummary`
  (+ `level` text already present); single source shared with hold-full.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — extract/reuse the level-up option builder so both
  paths stay in parity; `choice.ts` is the canonical builder.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `summariseWeaponLevelChange`: per-weapon
  applicability filter (no AoE delta on non-AoE weapons).
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — no behavioural change expected (it
  already renders `changeSummary`); verify only.
- Tests: `src/powerups/unlocks.test.ts`, `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` (shared-builder parity).

## Related work

- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool
  (completed; owner of `buildUpgradeOptions`).
- AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR — Show upgrade change summary + New badge in the
  hold-full choice list (completed; introduced `changeSummary` rendering).
- AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD — Upgrade and weapon descriptions (completed; item copy
  from shared catalogues).
- AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J — per-weapon level state (weapon level machinery).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — power-up level machine (parent of power-up levels).

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want an executable contract (failing tests) for the two level-scaling axes before any production code exists, so the curves, rounding rules and cap behaviour are pinned before implementation.

This is the test-first item for the `src/core/levelScaling.ts` module and the `GameRules` scaling data (AC "Data-driven level-scaling curves" and the unit-test part of AC "Tests" of the parent item AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Create `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts` (new file) and extend `src/core/rules.test.ts` with tests that pin the agreed contract. These tests must **fail on pre-change HEAD** because neither the module nor the rules fields exist yet.

Curve contract to pin:

- `enemyCountMultiplier(level)`: `1.0` at level 1, `2.0` at level 10, linear in between (assert the exact formula value at level 5, e.g. `1 + (level - 1) * (1.0 / 9)`), monotonically non-decreasing across 1–10.
- `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)`: `0.18` at level 1 (equal to the exported `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE`), `0.05` at level 10, monotonically non-increasing across 1–10, and `chance(10) <= 0.3 * chance(1)`.
- Extra Life proportionality: the small-asteroid Extra Life chance scales by the same ratio as the per-kill chance (`chance(level) / chance(1)`), so level 1 equals `rules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` exactly.
- Input clamping: levels below 1 clamp to 1, levels above the campaign maximum clamp to the maximum, and non-finite/non-integer inputs resolve to a documented clamped integer (no `NaN` output).
- Count application helper (`applyEnemyCountScaling` or the agreed equivalent): documented round-half-up rule, floor of 1, per-group safety cap of 200, `single`-formation groups left at exactly 1, and a level-1 identity transform (deep-equal input/output).
- Rules: the new scaling fields have documented defaults (1.0→2.0 multiplier, 0.18→0.05 drop chance), are clamped on load, and a legacy persisted blob without them loads with the defaults merged (backwards-compatible, no schema break).

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests exist and fail on pre-change HEAD for the specified reason (module/rules fields absent); record the failure output in a comment on this item.
- Tests cover monotonicity, clamping, level-1 identity, rounding rule, `single` groups, the 200 cap, Extra Life proportionality and legacy rules-blob merging.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).
- Every test name states the behaviour it pins; no asserts without a stated reason.

- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **Tests** — Unit tests cover curve monotonicity/clamping, count application (rounding, `single` groups, caps, L1 identity, seeded determinism), per-level drop chance, Extra Life proportionality and game↔gym parity. New tests fail on the pre-change code and pass after it.

## Key Files

- `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts` (new)
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None. Blocks the level-scaling implementation item.

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want the level-based gyms to run the same scaled counts and lengthened supply cadence as the game, so feedback from the gym is trustworthy.

Implements "Desired change" step 4 and the parent AC "Gym parity" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

- Pass the campaign level number through the gym launch data (`LevelDefinition.level` is already present in `GymLevelData`; single-wave launches use `0`).
- Apply the **same shared** count-scaling helper in `GymLevel` (consumed by `GymBotTuning`) — no divergent copy.
- Derive the gym's drop spawn interval from the level's drop chance: `interval(level) = interval(1) * chance(1) / chance(level)` in `_initSupplyLayer`.
- Pass the level number from `GymCurveSequencer._launchLevel` (already forwards `{ level }`); keep `_launchWave` at level 1 semantics.
- Add a code comment recording the documented divergence: formation gyms have no campaign-level context, so their fixed-cadence supply is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A level launched in `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` produces the same per-group counts as the game campaign for the same level.
- Supply cadence lengthens by the inverse drop-chance ratio; level 1 cadence is unchanged.
- Single-wave launches behave as level 1.
- The formation-gym divergence is recorded in a code comment and in the parent work item.
- The parity tests added by the test-first item pass and existing gym tests pass.
- `GymBoss`, `GymCentipede`, `GymFodderEnemies` and other formation gyms are unchanged.

- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **Gym parity** — The same scaling helper is used by the level-based gyms (`GymLevel`, hence `GymBotTuning`, and the curve-sequencer launch path) so a launched level produces the same enemy counts as the game, and the level-gym supply cadence is lengthened by the inverse drop-chance ratio so high-level gym runs are not over-supplied. Formation gyms keep their documented scene-specific supply source (no campaign level context) and are unchanged; the divergence is recorded in the work item and a code comment. A parity test asserts game campaign and level-gym counts match for the same level.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`
- `src/core/levelScaling.ts`

## Goal

**User story:** As a producer, I want the before/after bot-batch evidence and the scaling documentation in one place, so the change can be reviewed on evidence and future tuning has a written baseline.

Implements "Desired change" step 6 and the parent ACs "Automated balance evidence" and "Documentation" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

- Run a same-seed **baseline batch** (100 games, competent policy) with the level curves disabled (pre-change behaviour) and a **post-change batch**, using the extended per-level harness mode. Record both in the parent work item and in `docs/BALANCING.md`.
- Record per-level `powerUpsCollected`, `enemiesKilledByArchetype`, `avoidableHits`, `survivalSeconds` and `levelReached`; show mid/late-level power-up supply per enemy is below baseline and that the reached-level/completion metric does not regress and nothing crashes.
- If the evidence shows the endpoints are wrong, adjust the tuning data within the agreed curve shape (linear count ramp, monotonic non-increasing drop chance) and re-run; document the final values and the reason.
- Update `docs/BALANCING.md` (scaling table + evidence + how to reproduce), the GDD power-up and level sections, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` if the wave-build seam description changed, plus README/related docs references.
- Record the documented divergence for formation gyms (no campaign-level context) in the parent work item and alongside the code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Baseline and post-change batches are recorded with the per-level metrics listed above, the exact command and commit hashes, and the same seed set.
- Evidence shows lower per-kill power-up supply at mid/late levels than baseline and no fall in the reached-level/completion metric; no crash in either batch.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` documents the curves (table for levels 1–10), the rationale and how to reproduce the evidence.
- GDD power-up/level sections and any other affected docs/README references are updated.
- Docs assertions (`src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`, `evaluationDocs.test.ts`) pass.

The evidence must show the mid/late-level power-up supply per enemy is below baseline and that the campaign remains playable (no crash, no fall in the batch's reached-level/completion metric).
